FICTIONAL PATIENT FOR SOFTWARE TESTING ONLY

Patient: Synthetic Iris Vale
Age: 52 years
Clinic record number: SYN-IV-1017
Date of service: 17 October 2026
Treating clinician: Dr. Mara Keene
Visit type: In-person gastrointestinal outpatient office visit. This is an established patient.

History of present illness
Synthetic Iris Vale is being evaluated for heartburn present for three weeks. Burning rises behind the breastbone after meals and lasts about 12 minutes at a time. Swallowing and appetite are unchanged. She reports no difficulty swallowing, painful swallowing, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting blood, black stool, blood in the stool or unintended weight loss.
Her medical history is seasonal allergic rhinitis. She has never had abdominal surgery. She uses cetirizine 10 mg orally once daily as needed for allergy symptoms. A two-week trial of an over-the-counter antacid ended last month; she is no longer taking that antacid. Sulfonamide antibiotics cause a rash. Medications were reviewed and reconciled in the EHR today.
She has never smoked and does not use alcohol or recreational drugs. She is married and works as a librarian.

Review of systems
A 14-point review of systems was performed. There are no additional findings beyond the heartburn described above.

Examination
She is alert, oriented and in no distress. Her head is normocephalic, pupils are equal, sclerae are anicteric and the oropharynx is clear. Her neck is supple without lymphadenopathy. Lungs are clear bilaterally. Heart rhythm is regular without a murmur. The abdomen is soft and not distended, with normal bowel sounds and no tenderness, rebound or guarding. Her extremities are warm and well perfused without edema. She moves all limbs and has no focal neurologic deficit. Mood and affect are normal. The rectal examination was deferred.

Impression
Heartburn.

Plan
Upper endoscopy is requested for a later date if symptoms persist. Endoscopy was not performed today, no specimen was obtained and there are no investigation results from this visit. No procedure was performed today. She will avoid meals within three hours of bedtime and keep a symptom diary. No prescription is started today. Review is planned in three weeks. She should contact the clinic earlier for difficulty swallowing, bleeding, persistent vomiting or worsening symptoms.

Office E/M selection is based on total physician time on the date of service. Dr. Keene personally spent 32 minutes on the encounter date: four minutes reviewing the chart before the visit, 22 minutes directly with the patient obtaining history, examining and counseling her, and six minutes entering orders and documenting the visit. The 32 minutes exclude eight minutes of staff rooming and three minutes of physician preparation on the preceding day. They also exclude time for separately reported services.

tabular.introduction:
<introduction>
    <introSection type="title">
      <title>ICD-10-CM TABULAR LIST of DISEASES and INJURIES</title>
    </introSection>
    <introSection type="subtitle">
      <title>Instructional Notations</title>
    </introSection>
    <introSection type="instruction">
      <title>Includes:</title>
      <instruction>
        <note>The word 'Includes' appears immediately under certain categories to further define, or give examples of, the content of the category.</note>
      </instruction>
    </introSection>
    <introSection type="instruction">
      <title>Excludes Notes</title>
      <instruction>
        <note>The ICD-10-CM has two types of excludes notes.  Each note has a different definition for use but they are both similar in that they indicate that codes excluded from each other are independent of each other.</note>
      </instruction>
    </introSection>
    <introSection type="instruction">
      <title>Excludes1</title>
      <instruction>
        <note>A type 1 Excludes note is a pure excludes.  It means 'NOT CODED HERE!'  An Excludes1 note indicates that the code excluded should never be used at the same time as the code above the Excludes1 note.  An Excludes1 is used when two conditions cannot occur together, such as a congenital form versus an acquired form of the same condition.</note>
      </instruction>
    </introSection>
    <introSection type="instruction">
      <title>Excludes2</title>
      <instruction>
        <note>A type 2 excludes note represents 'Not included here'.  An excludes2 note indicates that the condition excluded is not part of the condition it is excluded from but a patient may have both conditions at the same time.  When an Excludes2 note appears under a code it is acceptable to use both the code and the excluded code together.</note>
      </instruction>
    </introSection>
    <introSection type="instruction">
      <title>Code First/Use Additional Code notes (etiology/manifestation paired codes)</title>
      <instruction>
        <note>Certain conditions have both an underlying etiology and multiple body system manifestations due to the underlying etiology.  For such conditions the ICD-10-CM has a coding convention that requires the underlying condition be sequenced first followed by the manifestation.  Wherever such a combination exists there is a 'use additional code' note at the etiology code, and a 'code first' note at the manifestation code.  These instructional notes indicate the proper sequencing order of the codes, etiology followed by manifestation.</note>
        <note>In most cases the manifestation codes will have in the code title, 'in diseases classified elsewhere.'  Codes with this title are a component of the etiology/ manifestation convention. The code title indicates that it is a manifestation code.  'In diseases classified elsewhere' codes are never permitted to be used as first listed or principal diagnosis codes. They must be used in conjunction with an underlying condition code and they must be listed following the underlying condition.</note>
      </instruction>
    </introSection>
    <introSection type="instruction">
      <title>Code Also</title>
      <instruction>
        <note>A code also note instructs that 2 codes may be required to fully describe a condition but the sequencing of the two codes is discretionary, depending on the severity of the conditions and the reason for the encounter.</note>
      </instruction>
    </introSection>
    <introSection type="instruction">
      <title>7th characters and placeholder X</title>
      <instruction>
        <note>For codes less than 6 characters that require a 7th character a placeholder X should be assigned for all characters less than 6.  The 7th character must always be the 7th character of a code</note>
      </instruction>
    </introSection>
  </introduction>

chapter:21.description: Factors influencing health status and contact with health services (Z00-Z99)

instructions.text: Z codes represent reasons for encounters. A corresponding procedure code must accompany a Z code if a procedure is performed. Categories Z00-Z99 are provided for occasions when circumstances other than a disease, injury or external cause classifiable to categories A00-Y89 are recorded as 'diagnoses' or 'problems'. This can arise in two main ways:

(a) When a person who may or may not be sick encounters the health services for some specific purpose, such as to receive limited care or service for a current condition, to donate an organ or tissue, to receive prophylactic vaccination (immunization), or to discuss a problem which is in itself not a disease or injury.
(b) When some circumstance or problem is present which influences the person's health status but is not in itself a current illness or injury.

chapter:18.description: Symptoms, signs and abnormal clinical and laboratory findings, not elsewhere classified (R00-R99)

instructions.text: This chapter includes symptoms, signs, abnormal results of clinical or other investigative procedures, and ill-defined conditions regarding which no diagnosis classifiable elsewhere is recorded.

Signs and symptoms that point rather definitely to a given diagnosis have been assigned to a category in other chapters of the classification. In general, categories in this chapter include the less well-defined conditions and symptoms that, without the necessary study of the case to establish a final diagnosis, point perhaps equally to two or more diseases or to two or more systems of the body. Practically all categories in the chapter could be designated 'not otherwise specified', 'unknown etiology' or 'transient'. The Alphabetical Index should be consulted to determine which symptoms and signs are to be allocated here and which to other chapters. The residual subcategories, numbered .8, are generally provided for other relevant symptoms that cannot be allocated elsewhere in the classification.
The conditions and signs or symptoms included in categories R00-R94 consist of:
(a) cases for which no more specific diagnosis can be made even after all the facts bearing on the case have been investigated;
(b) signs or symptoms existing at the time of initial encounter that proved to be transient and whose causes could not be determined;
(c) provisional diagnosis in a patient who failed to return for further investigation or care;
(d) cases referred elsewhere for investigation or treatment before the diagnosis was made;
(e) cases in which a more precise diagnosis was not available for any other reason;
(f) certain symptoms, for which supplementary information is provided, that represent important problems in medical care in their own right.
